# Design System v0.1 — COP32 companion platform (unofficial)
**Status: PROPOSED, Phase 21 Track C, 2026-10-03.** Machine-readable source: `tokens.json` (generated by `build_tokens.py`; the contrast table below is the script's real output — 46 checks, 0 failures). Components: `component-inventory.md`.

## 0. Identity and honesty notes
- **No brand identity was supplied by the founder.** This is an **original, neutral** palette (deep highland green, warm paper neutrals, ochre accent). It deliberately does **not** imitate any UNFCCC/COP visual identity, national flag arrangement, or government mark (D1, D3 risk flag). A host-supplied identity, if ever granted, would replace the colour tokens only.
- Every screen carries the "Independent platform — not an official COP32 product" label (IA §2.2, TRU-04).
- Basis: documentation + computed contrast. **Not** tested with real users, low-end screens or screen readers. See §10.

## 1. Principles (from D11, D16 v2, D21, D25–D27, IA second pass)
1. **Spacious and legible** — Ethiopian users report preferring spacious layouts over cluttered super-app screens; fewer items per screen, large targets.
2. **Amharic is not an afterthought** — own line-height ratio, expansion-safe labels, bundled font.
3. **Calm and trustworthy** — no ad-like banners at the top of Home, no autoplay carousels, no dark patterns (no fake urgency, no guilt copy, no pre-ticked consent; D21).
4. **Status is always visible** — source label, last-updated, offline/sync state, "TBC" as a first-class state.
5. **Never colour alone** — every status has an icon and a text label.
6. **Same structure on Android, iOS, web** (platform parity, D27); platform-native patterns only for navigation chrome.

Usage rules: `primary` = main actions, selected tab, key links of the app's own navigation; `accent` = one secondary emphasis per screen at most (e.g., "Live now" badge, never decorative); `info/success/warning/danger` pairs are used **only** for banners, alerts and status chips and always with an icon and text. Alerts (critical) use `danger`/`dangerBg` and are the only full-width coloured element permitted on Home. `border` is deliberately mid-tone (≥3:1) so controls are discoverable; `divider` is decorative only.

## 3. Typography
- **Family:** **Noto Sans Ethiopic** (variable: wght 100–900, wdth 62.5–100; SIL OFL 1.1; 860 mapped code points) — bundled in every client, **no reliance on OS fonts** (D11). The Latin letters, digits and common punctuation are covered by this same file (checked in the font's cmap), so one family renders mixed EN/AM strings consistently. **Not covered:** symbols such as ✓ → — use SVG icons only (sandbox finding, S1/F1, D49). Web: subset to Ethiopic + Basic Latin and serve as woff2 (target well under the 200 KB first-view budget; subset size **not yet measured**).
- **Weights:** 400 body, 500 labels, 600 headings, 700 emphasis. Avoid weights below 400 for Ge'ez.
- **Scale** (px at 100%; line-height ratios differ per script because Ge'ez is dense and tall):

| Style | Size | Line-height EN | Line-height AM |
|---|---|---|---|
| display | 28 | 1.25 | 1.45 |
| title | 22 | 1.3 | 1.5 |
| heading | 18 | 1.35 | 1.55 |
| body | 16 | 1.5 | 1.7 |
| bodySmall | 14 | 1.5 | 1.7 |
| label | 14 | 1.3 | 1.5 |
| caption | 12 | 1.4 | 1.6 |

- **Minimum:** body 16px; AM running text never < 14px. Honour OS text scale up to **200 %** without loss of content or function; layouts reflow, never truncate essential info (tab labels may wrap to two lines or switch to an icon-above-label stack with a 2-line cap).
- **Fallback stack:** `'Noto Sans Ethiopic', system-ui, sans-serif` — the system fallback exists only to avoid blank text if the font fails to load; releases are blocked on font-load checks.
- **Numerals and times:** Arabic numerals by default; 24h or explicit AM/PM with `EAT` shown (Ethiopian clock counting differs — explainer to be validated); Ethiopian calendar optional (Should).
- **Language tagging:** every text node carries `lang="am"|"en"` (screen-reader voice switching).

## 4. Spacing, grid, layout
- 4-px base; scale: 0, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64. Screen gutter 16; card padding 16; vertical rhythm 8/16/24.
- Content max width 720 on tablet/desktop (centered); phone is one column. Breakpoints: phone 0, tablet 600, desktop 960. Web uses top navigation at ≥ 960 and bottom tab bar below (same five destinations).
- Use **logical start/end** properties everywhere (RTL-ready for later Arabic, accessibility doc §3.2).

## 5. Shape, elevation, motion
- Radius: 6 (chips, inputs), 12 (cards, banners), 20 (sheets), pill (badges). Elevation: 0 / 1 (cards) / 2 (sheets, menus); in dark mode prefer surface tint over shadow.
- Motion: 120/200/320 ms, ease `cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1)`. With reduce-motion on: no transitions other than instant state change; never auto-play anything; nothing flashes.

## 6. Iconography
- One consistent outline icon set as **SVG**, 24px grid, 2px stroke, rounded joins, 48px minimum hit area. Candidate sources with permissive licences (Lucide — ISC; Material Symbols — Apache-2.0) **to be confirmed by licence check** before adoption; the prototype uses a handful of simple hand-drawn SVG paths.
- Icons never carry meaning alone: always a text label, except universally understood utility (search, close, back), which still get accessible names.
- Mirror directional icons in RTL; do not mirror logos, media controls, or clocks.

## 7. Accessibility annotations (D25–D27)
| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Target size | ≥ 48×48 dp Android, ≥ 44×44 pt iOS, ≥ 44 CSS px web (exceeds WCAG 2.2 minimum 24×24); ≥ 8 px between adjacent targets |
| Focus | Visible 3 px `focus` ring, 2 px offset, never removed; not obscured by sticky headers/tab bar (scroll-padding); logical order = visual order |
| Text scaling | Up to 200 % without clipping; fixed-height containers prohibited for text; tab bar grows; reflow at 320 CSS px (web) |
| Contrast | §2.1; re-check any new token pair with `build_tokens.py` |
| Colour | Never the only carrier of meaning; chips and banners include icon + text |
| Motion | `prefers-reduced-motion` / OS setting respected; no autoplay audio/video |
| Screen readers | Names, roles, states for every control; live-region announcements for alerts (assertive only for critical); Amharic TTS quality is uncertain → provide text and, for key content, recorded audio (Should) |
| Gestures | No path-based or multi-finger gestures required; swipe/drag always has a button alternative |
| Forms | Visible labels (not placeholders-only), inline errors with text, no time limits |
| Language | EN/AM switch in header on every screen; fall back visibly ("translation pending") |
| Low data | Text-first, images ≤ 100 KB, lazy, no autoplay video; Data-saver toggle (MVP setting) |
| Privacy-by-design (D21) | No manipulative nudges; notification and location prompts are explained first and refusable; consent controls are equal-weight (Allow / Not now) |

## 8. Platform notes
Android (Material 3 navigation bar, back gesture) and iOS (tab bar, swipe-back) follow native navigation conventions with these shared tokens; implementation in whichever framework S1 selects. Tokens are exported as JSON so Android/iOS/web codebases generate platform constants from one file instead of hand-copying.

## 9. How the prototype (Track D) uses this
CSS custom properties are generated from `tokens.json`; the prototype is the first consumer and therefore the first test of the spec.

## 10. Still needs real-world validation
- [ ] Ge'ez legibility at 14–16 px and at 200 % on real low-end Android screens and iPhones (S1 devices).
- [ ] Real users' reaction to palette, spacing density and tone (Addis residents and international visitors); colour-blindness simulation pass.
- [ ] TalkBack/VoiceOver behaviour with Amharic, focus order, announcements.
- [ ] Native-speaker review of all Amharic UI strings (none are final in this system).
- [ ] Icon set licence confirmation and cultural review of imagery.
- [ ] High-contrast theme; Ethiopian calendar/time presentation test.
- [ ] Subset font size measurement and web performance budget check.
- [ ] Legal/brand check if any host-provided identity is later offered.
